source_name: TED CPV browse (browse by sector) — banking/financial CPV families
why_relevant: Provides the controlled vocabulary anchor for the whole cell: CPV 66100000 banking and investment services, 66110000 banking services, 66172000 financial transaction processing / clearing-house services, 66600000 treasury services, plus adjacent IT CPVs (72200000, 48000000) that carry core-banking / card-system procurements.

source_name: EU Publications Office — public procurement procurement-details pages (op.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Publications Office mirrors individual procurement records (observed pattern .../procurement-details/-/procurement/{uuid}) and hosts TED reusers-workshop material explaining how to retrieve eForms notices — both a data surface and a methodology source.

source_name: Pályázati Portál — palyazat.gov.hu (Széchenyi Terv Plusz national EU-funds portal)
source_subtype: national managing-authority portal for EU funds
why_relevant: Central Hungarian portal for EU-cofinanced programmes 2021-2027 (Széchenyi Terv Plusz) and the RRF. Hosts calls (felhívások), programme documents and the managing-authority structure — the upstream layer that generates EU-funded procurements, including financial-instrument and digitalisation calls relevant to banking/payments vendors.

source_name: palyazat.gov.hu — Közbeszerzések (procurement section of the EU-funds portal)
why_relevant: Lists the managing authorities' own procurement procedures financed from technical assistance and programme budgets (translation, IT, advisory, financial services). Directly surfaces EU-funded contracts that rarely reach national media.

source_name: Támogatott projektkereső (supported-project search, palyazat.gov.hu)
why_relevant: Searchable register of awarded EU-funded projects (data drawn from EMIR / EUPR / IIER monitoring systems, updated daily) with beneficiary, programme, amount and region. Lets you identify banks, fintechs and payment-infrastructure beneficiaries and the projects that will trigger downstream procurement.

source_name: Magyarország Helyreállítási és Ellenállóképességi Terve (RRF / HET) pages
why_relevant: Hungary's Recovery and Resilience Plan components (digitalisation, education, health) drive large EU-financed procurements; several have payment/e-administration and financial-IT elements. The plan and its component documents identify responsible institutions and milestone-linked spending.

source_name: Kohesio — EU cohesion policy project & beneficiary platform
source_subtype: EU open data platform / project register
why_relevant: EU-level, harmonised register of ERDF/CF/ESF-funded projects and beneficiaries across member states, including Hungary, with CSV/XLSX and RDF datasets. Enables cross-checking Hungarian EU-funded beneficiaries in the financial-sector value chain against national data.

source_name: Cohesion Open Data Platform (DG REGIO)
why_relevant: Programme-level financial allocation and implementation data per member state and priority. Useful for sizing the EU-funded budget envelopes (incl. financial instruments) behind Hungarian banking-adjacent procurement pipelines.

source_name: Opentender.eu — Hungary portal (Government Transparency Institute / DIGIWHIST)
why_relevant: Cleaned, harmonised and deduplicated procurement dataset combining TED (above-threshold) with the Hungarian national portal (Közbeszerzési Hatóság) below-threshold data, plus buyer/supplier profiles and integrity indicators. Excellent for supplier-share and incumbency analysis that raw TED does not offer.

source_name: data.europa.eu — TED and Kohesio dataset entries
why_relevant: Official EU open data portal cataloguing TED CSV subsets, Kohesio linked data and related procurement datasets with distribution links and update cadence — the canonical pointer for machine-readable EU procurement duplicates of Hungarian notices.

source_name: European Commission Financial Transparency System (FTS)
why_relevant: Searchable database of recipients of directly-managed EU budget funds, including Hungarian entities. Complements shared-management data (Széchenyi/RRF) by exposing EU-level contracts and grants awarded to Hungarian financial-sector and fintech actors.

source_name: EU Funding & Tenders Portal (SEDIA)
why_relevant: Single entry point for calls and procurements managed directly by the Commission and its agencies. Hungarian banks, payment processors and IT vendors appear both as applicants and as contractors; also carries DG-level financial-services procurement that shapes the regional market.

source_name: MFB (Magyar Fejlesztési Bank) GINOP Plusz financial-instrument programme pages
why_relevant: EU-cofinanced financial instruments (GINOP Plusz-1.4.3-24, 1.4.4-24, 1.4.5-25 etc.) are distributed through selected commercial-bank intermediaries (observed: MBH Bank, OTP, Gránit). Intermediary selection and product mechanics are an EU-funded, banking-specific channel that never shows as a classic tender but reshapes bank distribution economics.

source_name: Korm. rendelet 373/2022. (IX. 30.) on the implementation of Hungary's RRP (net.jogtar.hu)
why_relevant: Legal basis naming the responsible institutions and the procurement-control regime for RRF-funded contracts in Hungary (incl. the role of NFK in vetting procurement procedures). Defines which bodies act as contracting authorities — the entity list to filter TED on.

source_name: Portfolio.hu — banking and EU-funds coverage (pointer/indirect)
why_relevant: Leading Hungarian financial-news outlet that reports changes in EU-funded credit programmes, intermediary bank arrangements and large public financial-services contracts, often earlier and with more context than official notices. Serves as a lead generator for TED lookups.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB) – hivatalos portál
why_relevant: Home of Hungary's public procurement remedies tribunal (KDB), the primary first-instance body deciding appeals against banking/payment-services tenders (account management, card acceptance, POS, cash logistics). Acts as the master pointer to decisions, pending applications, ex-officio initiations and the related court judgments.

source_name: Döntőbizottsági határozatok (KDB decisions listing)
why_relevant: Full text KDB decisions (D.xxx/yyyy numbering) naming contracting authority, bidders, contested evaluation criteria, prices and the outcome (annulment, fine, rejection). For banking/payments this is the richest disclosure layer behind an award notice.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Döntőbizottsági és bírósági határozatok adatbázis (structured search)
why_relevant: The structured, filterable database of KDB AND court decisions. Verified by fetch that it exposes ~20+ filters: case number (ügyiratszám), contracting authority and applicant names, procedure type, decision type and date ranges, subject matter, legal basis, court decision number, EU preliminary-ruling flag, CPV codes and tags. CPV filtering (66xxxxxx financial/insurance services) makes banking/payments extraction tractable.

source_name: KDB – Jogorvoslati kérelmek (pending remedy applications)
why_relevant: Early-warning layer: applications filed but not yet decided. Signals a contested banking/payments tender weeks-to-months before the decision and before any contract-award correction notice appears.

source_name: Fővárosi Törvényszék judgments published as KDB case attachments
why_relevant: The Fővárosi Törvényszék has exclusive jurisdiction over judicial review of KDB decisions; its judgments are mirrored as attachments on the KDB site under a predictable attachment path with case numbers such as 103.K.704.694/2024/10 linked to D.634/2024. Judgments often restate bid prices and evaluation detail and show whether an award was ultimately annulled.

source_name: Bírósági Határozatok Gyűjteménye (BHGY) – national court decisions collection
why_relevant: Statutory collection of anonymised judgments including administrative-litigation judgments on single-instance administrative decisions — the category that covers KDB judicial review. Full-text indexed with statute-based and free-text search, so 'Kbt.' + banking terms can be searched directly.

source_name: Kúria – anonimizált határozatok / precedent decisions
why_relevant: Supreme court (Kúria) review (felülvizsgálat, Kfv. numbering) sets the doctrine that shapes how banking/payment procurement disputes are decided, and its own case pages include preliminary-reference cases such as Kfv.III.37.415/2017 arising from the interchange-fee litigation.

source_name: Gazdasági Versenyhivatal (GVH) – Döntések adatbázis
why_relevant: Hungarian Competition Authority decision database. Covers bid-rigging (kartell) cases in public tenders and payments-sector conduct cases. Confirmed to contain the landmark Vj-018/2008 multilateral interchange fee cartel decision against 22 banks plus Visa and Mastercard (fines >HUF 1.9bn), and consumer-protection cases against POS-terminal vendors.

source_name: GVH ágazati vizsgálat – bankkártya-elfogadási piac jelentés (2019 sector inquiry)
why_relevant: Sector inquiry report into the Hungarian card-acceptance market: acquirer shares, merchant fee structures, terminal deployment. Directly relevant background for interpreting acquiring/POS tenders and for identifying the acquirer set that bids on public contracts.

source_name: GVH Sajtószoba (press releases)
why_relevant: Fastest signal that a payments/banking competition case has opened or closed, often naming the undertaking before the full decision text is published (e.g. the case against a POS-terminal installer company).

source_name: Állami Számvevőszék (ÁSZ) – Jelentések
why_relevant: State Audit Office report library. ÁSZ audits of public bodies routinely test procurement lawfulness and contract management, including financial-service contracts (account management, treasury), and it has audited the MNB and EUTAF. Reports name entities, amounts and specific procurement failures.

source_name: ÁSZ közérdekű adatok – saját szerződések és beszerzések
why_relevant: ÁSZ itself publishes its service-procurement and asset-sale contracts above the statutory threshold, and its own management is audited by an auditor selected through public procurement — a small but concrete example of the public-body contract-disclosure layer that also applies to banking service contracts.
